reason: Conversation 1 reached the key sensible step: it told the homeowner to unplug and then clean the hidden sump compartment, which produced a real improvement (60 min vs 20-40 min), and it closed by escalating to an engineer and asking for the full model number before any part. Its weaknesses were two wasted turns (the 'is the drum warm' test the customer rightly challenged, and an emergency-drain-hose check the customer couldn't do) and a somewhat over-confident lean toward 'blocked or failed pump' without naming the level switch as an alternative, though it never named a part number. Conversation 2 was safe and honest but gave up after a single exchange, never pointing to the pump sump cleaning that the ground truth identifies as the core DIY step, so the homeowner was left with a premature engineer referral and no improvement.
